theme: Cosmic Inversion, Collapse of the Social Hierarchy, and Sovereign Decree of the Divine
historical_context: Composed in response to the revolutionary upheaval of 18th-century Punjab. The decline of the Mughal aristocracy, the peasant uprisings of the Banda Singh Bahadur era, and the rise of Dalit, lower-caste, and Sikh Misls completely overturned feudal norms. Bulleh observes this revolution without bourgeois grief: crows hunt falcons, sparrows devour hawks, and thoroughbred Iraqi steeds are whipped while donkeys graze on lush clover. Recognizing that this social upheaval is commanded from the Divine Court ('हुकम हज़ूरों आया'), Bulleh accepts this holy inversion as Divine Justice against tyrannical elites.

original: कां लगड़ नूं मारन लग्गे चिड़ियां जुर्रे खाए,
stanzas.hindi_gloss: उलटे (विपरीत/उलटे) होर (और भी विचित्र) ज़माने (युग/दिन) आए (आ पहुँचे हैं)। कां (कौवे) लगड़ नूं (शिकारी बाज/फाल्कन को) मारन लग्गे (मारने लगे हैं), चिड़ियां (नन्हीं गौरैया चिड़ियाँ) जुर्रे (शिकारी शिकारी बाजों को) खाए (मार-मार कर खा रही हैं)।
stanzas.english_gloss: उलटे होर ज़माने आए (Inverted, topsy-turvy times have arrived). कां (Crows) लगड़ नूं (falcons) मारन लग्गे (have begun to strike and kill), चिड़ियां (fragile sparrows) जुर्रे खाए (devour mighty hunting hawks).
poetic_hindi: कौवे बाज को मारन लागे, चिड़ियाँ शिकरे खाए,
poetic_english: Topsy-turvy times have come to pass!
Crows strike down the falcon fast, sparrows eat the hawks at last,
Topsy-turvy times have come to pass!

original: इराकियां नूं पई चाबक पउंदी गद्धो खोद पवाए,
stanzas.hindi_gloss: इराकियां नूं (उच्च नस्ल के इराकी अरबी घोड़ों पर) पई चाबक पउंदी (चाबुकों की मार पड़ रही है), गद्धो (और गधों को) खोद (हरी-हरी दूब/घास की क्यारियों में) पवाए (चरने के लिए मखमली आसन दिए जा रहे हैं)।
stanzas.english_gloss: इराकियां नूं (Noble Iraqi steeds) पई चाबक पउंदी (are lashed with whips), गद्धो (while lowly donkeys) खोद पवाए (are fed rich pasture and pampering).
poetic_hindi: इराकी घोड़ों पे चाबुक बरसे, गधे हरी घास चबाए,
poetic_english: Iraqi thoroughbreds feel the whip, while donkeys feast and clover sip,
Topsy-turvy times have come to pass!

original: बुल्ल्हा हुकम हज़ूरों आया तिस नूं कौन हटाए,
stanzas.hindi_gloss: बुल्ल्हा (बुल्लेशाह कहता है) हुकम (यह क्रांति और युग-परिवर्तन का आदेश) हज़ूरों (सर्वोच्च परमात्मा के दरबार से) आया (आया है), तिस नूं (उस सर्वशक्तिमान आदेश को) कौन (कौन मनुष्य) हटाए (रोक या टाल सकता है?)।
stanzas.english_gloss: बुल्ल्हा (Bulleh cries) हुकम हज़ूरों आया (this sovereign decree has arrived from the Supreme Court on high), तिस नूं कौन हटाए (who possesses the power to avert it?).
poetic_hindi: बुल्ल्हा! हुक्म हुज़ूर से आया, इसे कौन लौटाए?
poetic_english: Bulleh cries: this edict came from God's Court above, who can defame?
Topsy-turvy times have come to pass!

sufi_commentary: Kafi 149 is a sharp sociopolitical and cosmic commentary on historical inversion (Inqilab / Ulat-pulaat). During the mid-18th century in Punjab, the decadent Mughal feudal nobility was smashed by peasant revolts, Afghan incursions, and the rise of local subaltern warriors. Bulleh captures this cataclysm through traditional ornithological and equestrian metaphors: the aristocratic hunters (the lagar-falcon, the jurra-hawk, and the thoroughbred Iraqi horse) are stripped of their supremacy, while the downtrodden (the crow, the sparrow, and the donkey) rise to power. Most orthodox chroniclers mourned this as the end of civilization; Bulleh Shah, however, recognizes it as a manifestation of Divine Irony and Cosmic Retribution: 'बुल्ल्हा हुकम हज़ूरों आया तिस नूं कौन हटाए'. When earthly tyrants exceed their measure, the Divine will inverts the cosmos, empowering sparrows to devour falcons.
title: उलटे होर ज़माने आए
